2025.note: Windstorm on the Saturday closed the Gate; the backlog held 6–8h for a full day.

2024.note: Rain closed the Gate for ~12h on the Friday, but once open it stayed under ~1h.

2022.note: First full-size year after the pandemic pause. Sparse coverage — treat as indicative.

2019.note: The last pre-pandemic year, and the cleanest weather of the set.

2018.note: Recovered from archived posts; mostly the early-arrival and opening days.

insights.text: Opening Sunday is the least predictable day of the week: a typical 6h 40m in 2025 versus 1h in 2024. The difference was weather, not demand — treat the two years as separate scenarios rather than averaging them.
Wait times during the first 36 hours after opening can be five or more hours.
If you can arrive Tuesday or later, you will find your wait time to be much shorter.
On all days but opening night, the shortest lines are usually in the early morning hours, generally from 3 a.m.-10 a.m.
Heavy traffic and longer wait times indeed happen Saturday, Sunday and Monday.
Gate Road travel times during Exodus peaked at six to nine hours just to get from Greeters to the pavement of County Road 34.
Allow up to 12 hours to reach the Reno airport during peak egress (Exodus).
Best exodus windows: try to leave very early in the morning, in the later evening, or on Tuesday morning before noon.
For 2026 Burning Man is aiming for a maximum ingress travel time - from the gravel to the Gate - of four hours whenever possible.
Waits of 6+ hours once you get to the playa are common at peak arrival hours (Sunday mid-day through Tuesday night, with ebbs and flows within that time period).
If you arrive from about Wednesday onwards, you're not going to have any real problems with entry lines.
Even if you have Early Entry passes you can still expect to wait half an hour to a couple hours at gate.
In 2014, some people waited upwards of 18 hours in line after the gate was closed due to rain.

Arriving before the 12:01am opening is actively punished: early arrivals without credentials are staged behind on-time drivers. In 2019, arriving at 11:49pm meant ~5 hours; arriving one minute later meant 25 minutes.
2023 was the mud-year anomaly: the driving ban meant Exodus, not ingress, was the extreme. Exodus ran 5h10m -> 6h -> 8h through Monday Sept 4 evening and was still ~7.5h Tuesday morning.
2024 opening was weather-shifted: the gate closed for rain and reopened around 3:15pm Saturday, roughly 12 hours after closure, with ~20,000 people waiting.

2025 was the worst modern ingress year in this dataset: an Aug 23 windstorm (45-50+ mph gusts) closed the gate, and the backlog produced 6-9 hour official waits through Monday Aug 25 and into Tuesday Aug 26.
Reported wait is self-defeating: when the reported Gate Road travel time is low, many folks choose that moment to leave, which can increase those times faster than they can be reported.
More than one third of Burners arrive on the first Monday of the event; a quarter still arrive after Monday, peaking again on the Thursday.
Early Arrival (work access) holders are ~12% of the population and enter before 6pm Sunday; in 2018 the Early-Arrival-only line still ran 2-4 hours on the Thursday/Friday/Saturday before opening.

Averaged over 2014-2017, ingress wait peaks roughly 18-26 hours after the gate opens (Sunday evening into Monday pre-dawn) at about 5 hours, is near zero in the first 2-4 hours after opening, and shows a second smaller ~2.5h bump around 58-62 hours after opening.
Averaged over 2014-2017, Exodus wait is low until the Temple burn (~24h after Man burn), then rises to a 3-4 hour plateau across the following 12-36 hours.
2024 ingress collapsed to a flat 20-minute floor from event Wednesday onward and never exceeded 30 minutes from Thursday to Burn Saturday.
2025 ingress stayed at or above 6 hours from Opening Sunday 09:00 through Tuesday 06:00 almost continuously, peaking at 8h40m on Monday 10:00.
Exodus peaks Sunday night (Temple Sunday ~20:00-23:00) and again Monday evening; the Tuesday-after window collapses to ~25-45 minutes.
BMIR 94.5 / GARS 95.1 FM broadcast hourly Gate Road wait reports at the top of the hour; @bmantraffic posts the same numbers, which is why hourly series exist at all.
